summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image for a Docusaurus website with three stages: a base Node.js image with common setup, a development stage where a user can work on the site, and a production stage that builds the site and serves it through nginx. The file uses build arguments to customize the user ID, group ID, and username for development work, and to control whether the image targets development or production environments.

explanations.5: HOMEDIR is a variable being set to /opt/docusaurus so it can be reused throughout the file instead of typing the path repeatedly.
explanations.6: TARGET is being set as a variable to distinguish between 'development' and 'production' modes, which is used later for different build steps.
explanations.9: DOCKER_UID sets the numeric user ID for the new user created in the container; 1000 is the standard first non-root user ID on Linux.
explanations.15: This creates a new stage called 'base' from the official Node.js long-term support image, which will be reused by the development and production stages.
explanations.18: FORCE_COLOR=0 tells yarn (the package manager) not to colorize its output, making logs cleaner and more reliable.
explanations.21: Corepack is a Node.js tool that lets you use specific package managers like yarn; enabling it ensures the right tool version is available.
explanations.24: This modifies the bash prompt (PS1) to show a ship emoji, the environment type, username, and current directory whenever someone opens a terminal in the container.
explanations.30: This creates a second stage called 'development' that inherits from 'base', which will set up an interactive development environment.
explanations.34: apt-get -y update refreshes the package list, then installs git without prompting (--yes) and removes unnecessary packages to keep the image small.
explanations.36: Git won't normally allow operations on directories it doesn't own; this tells it to trust the HOMEDIR directory even if the user IDs don't match.
explanations.46: This checks if DOCKER_UID is not equal to 1000; only if it's different does it create a custom user (otherwise the default node user with ID 1000 is used).
explanations.48: useradd creates a new user with the specified home directory, user ID, group ID, and shell—mimicking your host machine's user so file permissions match.
explanations.52: USER switches the container to run as the specified username instead of root, making development safer by preventing accidental system changes.
explanations.61: This creates a third stage called 'building_production' that starts fresh from 'base' and will compile the Docusaurus site for production.
explanations.66: NODE_ENV is set to the TARGET value (e.g., 'production') so that npm packages and the build process behave appropriately for production.
explanations.70: This runs the Docusaurus installer to scaffold a complete website structure in the HOMEDIR path using the classic template.
explanations.73: chown -R node:node changes ownership of all files from root to the 'node' user, since they were created by the root npm process.
explanations.82: yarn install --immutable ensures that exact versions of all dependencies are installed, making the build reproducible each time.
explanations.88: yarn build compiles the Docusaurus website from source into static HTML/CSS/JS files in the build directory.
explanations.94: This creates the final 'production' stage using a lightweight nginx image, which will serve the prebuilt website.
explanations.97: apk (Alpine's package manager) is updated and bash is installed; the cache is then removed to keep the final image small.
explanations.107: This copies only the finished website files (the build output) from the building_production stage into the nginx web directory, so only the finished product is in the final image.
